picks.rationale: Cincinnati's offense has been anemic recently, posting a 74 wRC+ over the last 30 days, which is the second-worst mark in Major League Baseball. While Great American Ball Park is known as a hitter-friendly venue, both starting pitchers, Michael McGreevy (3.48 ERA) and Brady Singer (4.66 ERA), have shown periods of effectiveness. The Cardinals' offense, though better than the Reds', is not explosive, ranking 18th in wRC+ over the past month. This combination of struggling offenses and decent pitching points towards a lower-scoring game, making the Under 10.5 a confident pick.

The Athletics are in a severe slump, having lost 16 of their last 20 games and already dropping the first three games of this series to the Royals. Kansas City will send RHP Randy Dobnak (2-1, 1.73 ERA) to the mound, who has been excellent this season, while the Athletics counter with LHP Gage Jump (5-7, 4.50 ERA). The Royals won the previous game 9-5, demonstrating their offensive capability against a struggling Athletics team. Given the Athletics' poor form and the pitching mismatch, the Royals are well-positioned to secure a comfortable win and cover the run line at favorable odds.

The White Sox boast an MLB-best 76-50 record against the Run Line this season, indicating their strong performance in covering spreads. Their starting pitcher, Anthony Kay (9-5, 4.01 ERA), has been remarkably consistent, not allowing more than three earned runs in any of his last ten starts. Conversely, Braves starter Grant Holmes (7-5, 3.82 ERA) was torched for six earned runs in his most recent outing, and the Braves' offense has struggled, scoring only seven runs in their last three games. This combination of White Sox's strong ATS record, Kay's reliability, and the Braves' recent offensive and pitching woes makes the White Sox +1.5 a confident pick.

Yankees ace Gerrit Cole (6-6, 3.23 ERA) has been in dominant form, not allowing more than two runs in any of his starts for nearly a month. Orioles starter Kyle Bradish (7-11, 3.69 ERA) also held the Yankees scoreless over six innings in their last head-to-head matchup. Furthermore, the Under has a strong trend when the Yankees play as road favorites, with a 37-18-2 record in such situations. While the Yankees' bullpen might be fatigued after pitching ten innings in the last two games, Cole's ability to go deep into games and Bradish's past success against New York support a low-scoring affair.

While Jacob deGrom (8-8, 3.95 ERA) is a formidable pitcher for the Rangers, he is coming off a start where he left due to triceps fatigue and is pitching on extra rest, raising questions about his full effectiveness. The Nationals, despite their overall record, just secured a dominant 6-0 shutout victory, with their starter Cade Cavalli striking out 11. The Rangers have been struggling recently, dropping out of a wild card spot and losing four of their last five games. Given deGrom's potential health concerns and the Rangers' recent poor form, the Nationals are a solid bet to keep this game within one run.
